wiring.label: Wiring board
legend: Red = +24 V, black = Ground, sensor wires keep their own colours

props.name: 24 V power supply plugs into J1 (outside)

steps.title: Connect power in and Ground
steps.note: Mount the rail, the StamPLC and the Wago connectors, then connect power in and Ground. Connectors: DC jack J1: + red, − black; inline fuse holder FU1: lead 1 red, lead 2 red; power button Q1: IN red, GND black. Press an M3 heat-set insert into each of the two rail pads in the base (soldering iron, straight down, flush with the pad) and screw the rail on from above with an M3×6 pan-head screw and a washer. Clip the StamPLC on the rail, front towards the lid. Clip the Wagos into the rack on the front wall, wire entries up, levers towards the unit, left to right: X-24, X-0V1, X-0V2, X-S, X-V. Put a ferrule on every wire end that goes under a screw. Pass each cable that leaves the box through the oval exit before you strip it. Unplug the supply and disconnect the air. J1: wire 1 on the centre-pin lug (+); with three lugs, wire 3 on the one that stays connected to the sleeve with the plug in (meter). Solder lugs: solder and heat-shrink. FU1 sits in the lead from J1 to Q1; the fuse goes in last. Wire 5 joins the two Ground Wagos. Every slot of a Wago is connected to all the others: use one wire per slot. Check with a meter: the centre pin of the plug is +24 V.

connections.la: DC jack J1 + (+24 V, centre pin)

steps.title: Connect the StamPLC
steps.note: Connect the power button Q1 to the +24 V Wago X-24, then the StamPLC to X-24 and to Ground. Connectors: power button Q1: OUT red; StamPLC: + red, − black, C black. Q1 is the lit POWER rocker. IN and OUT are the two connectors that connect when it is switched on, GND is the third (wire 6 on GND shorts the supply). Flat tabs: insulated receptacles. Wire 4 gives the Q1 lamp its Ground. Terminal C of the StamPLC is the common of all eight inputs: it goes to Ground (wire 9), which suits PNP sensors. Check: POWER off, the Q1 lamp stays dark (lit: swap wires 2 and 6). Then insert the fuse, POWER on: the StamPLC starts and shows its screen. POWER off.

steps.title: Connect E-STOP and the pressure switch
steps.note: Connect X-24 through the E-STOP and the pressure switch to the valve rail, and report both rails to the StamPLC. Connectors: E-STOP button: terminal 1 red, terminal 2 red; pressure switch QPM11: terminal 1 red, terminal 2 red; StamPLC: input 3 red, input 4 red. The valve rail X-V is live only while POWER is on, E-STOP is released and the air pressure is below the trip. E-STOP uses its closed contact: terminals 1 and 2, marked 11 and 12 on the contact block. Pressure switch QPM11: both cores of its cable are on the +24 V side (red) and it has no polarity; with no air, a meter must beep across its two terminals (closed contact type). The StamPLC inputs 3 and 4 only read the two rails: input 3 on shows E-STOP released, input 4 on shows the pressure is fine. An input accepts either polarity, it only needs the voltage between the input and C. E-STOP and the pressure switch cut only the valve rail: the StamPLC stays powered and shows the fault. Check: POWER on, air off: inputs 3 and 4 on; press E-STOP: both off.

steps.title: Connect the end sensors
steps.note: Connect the two end sensors. Connectors: StamPLC: input 1 black, input 2 black. Keep each sensor's own wire colours: brown wire = +24 V from X-24, blue wire = Ground, black wire = signal. These are PNP sensors: check the label SMT-8M-A-PS-… (PS = PNP). B0 reports home on input 1, B1 reports front on input 2. The signal wire drives the StamPLC input directly. If an input reads on with its sensor off (leakage current of the sensor), add a 4.7 kΩ resistor from that input to C. Position: B0 so input 1 is on with the rod fully home, B1 so input 2 is on 2–3 mm before the press bottoms.

steps.title: Connect the valve coils
steps.note: Connect the two valve coils through their plugs and relays 1 and 2 of the StamPLC. Connectors: valve plug Y1: pin 1 red, pin 2 black; valve plug Y2: pin 1 red, pin 2 black; StamPLC: relay 1 NC red, relay 1 COM red, relay 1 NO red, relay 2 COM red, relay 2 NO red. Y1 extends; Y2 retracts. Pin 1 is +24 V (red): mark that core at both ends of each valve cable. Relay terminals are NC, COM and NO: follow the labels on the unit, they are not in the order of this drawing. Relay 1 COM comes from the valve rail X-V, relay 1 NC feeds relay 2 COM, so relay 1 and 2 can never switch the two coils on together. Inside each plug, fit D7/D8 with the cores: ring on pin 1 (+), plain leg on pin 2; reversed, they short the supply. Leave them out only if the plug's datasheet shows built-in suppression (an LED alone is not enough). The plugs fit either coil: with air on, press the red manual button next to each coil; the coil that drives the rod out gets plug Y1. Check without air, meter on the plug pins, with the bench program (firmware/bench) toggling the relays: both off, neither plug is live; relay 1 on, only Y1 is live; relay 2 on, only Y2 is live; both on, only Y1 is live.

connections.la: StamPLC relay 1 NO (closed when the relay is on)
StamPLC relay 2 NO (closed when the relay is on)

steps.title: Supply → filter-regulator
steps.note: Mount the FRL upright on its bracket at the board edge, bowls hanging vertically and drains pointing down off the board, away from the control box. Follow the arrow on the FRL body. Supply: 7–10 bar; start with the regulator at 2 bar. If the unit has a lubricator, leave it empty: the cylinder and the valve are greased for life, and once you oil them you have to keep oiling. Check: Hose retained; FRL flow arrow points towards the valve.

steps.title: Filter-regulator → shut-off
steps.note: Fit the 3/2 shut-off with exhaust right after the FRL, its arrow pointing away from the FRL. Closed, it cuts the supply and vents everything after it: tee, pressure switch, valve and cylinder. Close it whenever you reach into the press. Check: Arrow points away from the FRL; exhaust port open, not plugged.

steps.title: Shut-off → pressure-switch tee
steps.note: Connect the shut-off outlet to the 6 mm tee. The QPM11 sits on the tee's branch and measures the regulated supply pressure. Set it to open at 6 bar: regulator at 6 bar (only for this setting), E-STOP released, POWER on with the bench image on the StamPLC: the fourth mark on its IN line shows 1. Turn the screw until it shows -, then set the regulator back to 5.5 bar or less. Check: Pressure switch after the shut-off; tee branch sealed.

steps.title: Tee → valve supply
steps.note: Connect the tee to P, the supply port. Read the letters on the valve body: never connect the supply to R or S (the exhausts). Check: Tube reaches P; no tight bend or kink.

steps.title: Valve A → cylinder cap end
steps.note: Connect A to the end without the rod. Fit a meter-out flow control: free flow into the cylinder, restricted flow out. This cap-end adjuster controls retraction speed. Start with both flow controls 1 turn open. Check: A reaches the cap end; flow-control direction confirmed.

steps.title: Valve B → cylinder rod end
steps.note: Connect B to the port beside the rod. Again use meter-out orientation. This rod-end adjuster controls extension speed. Leave room for cylinder movement. Check: B reaches the rod end; tube cannot rub or pull tight.

steps.title: Fit both exhaust silencers
steps.note: Fit one silencer to each exhaust and point both away from the control box and the operator. Do not cap or join these ports to supply. First air-on, POWER off: nothing may move and the lever must stay free by hand. If the rod creeps out, the valve is not exhaust-centre: close the shut-off. Check: Both exhausts open through silencers; no obstruction.
